title: Gunnunks
summary: Gunnunks is a Montauk North Neck placename for a swamp and nearby tract called Gunnunk's Garden, placed midway between Fort Pond and Culloden Point, at the foot of Rocky Ridge.
address_label: General North Neck / Rocky Ridge area, Montauk, NY
history_content: The history preserves local Montauk knowledge for Gunnunks, including information from Jonathan Gould before the surviving text breaks off. Stone's Montauk place-name index also lists Gunnunks among descriptive East Hampton Indian place names.
translation_content:
Recorded forms include Gunnunks and Gunnunk's Garden. The related Gonux entry connects the linguistic root with words for long, tall, high, or a tall person.

Why Place Names Matter

“The histories of the state’s traditionally associated tribes are embedded in places and place names.”

— J. Willard Marriott Library, Restoring Indigenous Place Names (2021), project description
land_loss_content: Gunnunks preserves a small Montauk landscape name tied to swamp, garden, ridge, and oral local knowledge. Recording it with uncertainty keeps the name visible while avoiding an invented exact boundary.
whereintheworld_content: Tooker places Gunnunks between Fort Pond and Culloden Point at the foot of Rocky Ridge. Its exact location remains uncertain.
